premises.protagonist: A 36-year-old cave surveyor maps systems that flood every spring and has never lost a team member.
premises.situation: Her team is two days from the entrance when the rain arrives early and the only exit is a passage she has not finished surveying.
premises.conflict: The unfinished passage may dead-end, and the injured member cannot survive the long route.
premises.setting: A limestone cave system in a monsoon region, present day.
premises.stakes: Four lives, her record, and the survey that justifies the expedition.

premises.protagonist: A 58-year-old skipper delivers other people's yachts across oceans and has stopped asking why.
premises.situation: He takes a three-week crossing with three strangers and a radio that only receives.
premises.conflict: The owner's instructions and the weather router disagree, and one of the crew is not who the paperwork says.
premises.setting: The North Atlantic, present day.
premises.stakes: The boat, the four of them, and the delivery fee that is his pension.

premises.setting: A hotel conference suite in a market town, present day.
premises.stakes: Her job, his dignity, and a crate of prize marrows.

premises.protagonist: A 48-year-old wedding officiant was ordained online and has just discovered the denomination requires quarterly reports.
premises.situation: The reports ask for details of ceremonies he performed from memory in a field.
premises.conflict: Filing honestly dissolves the denomination; filing badly means an audit of every wedding he has done.
premises.setting: A rural county with one registry office, present day.
premises.stakes: Four hundred marriages, his licence, and a couple whose wedding was in a barn.

premises.protagonist: A 29-year-old veterinary technician, six months divorced, agrees to share custody of the dog with her ex-husband's new partner.
premises.situation: The dog is diagnosed with a condition that gives it a year, and the shared calendar becomes the only structure either of them has.
premises.conflict: They are falling for each other while the animal that brought them together is dying.
premises.setting: A small mountain town with one vet practice, present day.
premises.stakes: The friendship that makes the dog's last year bearable, and the ex-husband's forgiveness.

premises.protagonist: A 26-year-old sign-language interpreter is assigned to a deaf comedian's farewell tour.
premises.situation: Twelve cities, six weeks, and a performer who is losing his sight as well as his hearing.
premises.conflict: Her professional code forbids the relationship, and the tour is his last chance to be seen on his own terms.
premises.setting: A twelve-city club circuit, present day.
premises.stakes: Her certification, his farewell, and the two people who understand the material.

premises.protagonist: A 24-year-old mapmaker's apprentice has spent six years copying coastlines that never move.
premises.situation: Her maps begin to change overnight, but only on the copies she keeps for herself.
premises.conflict: The guild burns inaccurate maps, and the changes are showing a road that does not exist yet.
premises.setting: A harbour city and the surveys of its hinterland, pre-industrial.
premises.stakes: Her apprenticeship, the guild's charter, and the town the road is heading for.

premises.protagonist: A 16-year-old beekeeper tends the hives that mark the valley's border and keep the passes closed.
premises.situation: The queen of the oldest hive stops laying, and the bees begin drifting into the next valley.
premises.conflict: The village elders want the hive burned, and the drift is the only sign of where her missing brother went.
premises.setting: A mountain valley with one road and one season, pre-industrial.
premises.stakes: The border, the harvest, and the last trace of her brother.

premises.protagonist: A 30-year-old widow runs her husband's printing press in a city where unlicensed presses are smashed.
premises.situation: A customer orders a pamphlet that names the men who ordered the last press destroyed.
premises.conflict: The job pays for her children's winter, and the customer is the man who signed her husband's warrant.
premises.setting: A European printing city, 1580s.
premises.stakes: The press, her children, and the record of what happened to her husband.

premises.protagonist: A 40-year-old midwife in a rural parish has attended every birth in three villages for twenty years.
premises.situation: A magistrate requires her to testify about a birth she attended in a house where the child later disappeared.
premises.conflict: The truth protects the mother and destroys the family that has fed her through every winter.
premises.setting: An agricultural parish, 1790s.
premises.stakes: A mother's life, the midwife's licence to practise, and the village's trust.

premises.protagonist: A 12-year-old is being bullied and has started eating lunch in the school boiler room.
premises.situation: A door in the boiler room opens into a copy of the school, one day behind.
premises.conflict: Everything she does there happens again tomorrow, and the people in it have started noticing her.
premises.setting: A comprehensive school in a small town, present day.
premises.stakes: Tomorrow, and the girl who will be blamed for what she does in it.

premises.stakes: Her hearing, her contract, and the thing the tape is counting down to.

premises.protagonist: A 58-year-old night-shift hospital cleaner keeps a notebook of the things patients say when they think no one is listening.
premises.situation: A new administrator begins shredding the ward logs she has been quietly rescuing from the recycling for years.
premises.conflict: The logs record a death her own family was told never happened, and the only copy is in a bag under her sink.
premises.setting: A mid-sized city hospital and the estate on its edge, present day.
premises.stakes: The only surviving account of what happened that night, and the job that pays for her mother's care.

premises.protagonist: A 67-year-old retired bus driver has rented the same flat for forty years and knows every neighbour by the sound of their door.
premises.situation: The building is sold, and the developer offers him a unit in the replacement tower on condition that he leaves quietly.
premises.conflict: Accepting saves him and helps empty the building of the people who cannot afford the tower.
premises.setting: A port city mid-redevelopment, present day.
premises.stakes: The neighbours' homes, and the version of himself he has been able to live with.

premises.conflict: The common thread is her employer's largest client, and the file that would prove it is the one she signed off on.
premises.setting: A drought-prone inland region over one summer, present day.
premises.stakes: Her career, and the next house on the pattern.

premises.situation: The voice on the tape describes a burglary at her own address, in detail, in the past tense.
premises.conflict: The burglary has not happened yet, and the police will not take a teenager seriously.
premises.setting: A commuter town with one bus an hour, present day.
premises.stakes: Her family's safety, and her grandfather, who owns the coat.

premises.situation: A fragment's trajectory implies a launch that no agency logged and a payload that never came down.
premises.conflict: The fragment is on a decay path toward a crewed station, and the audit that would flag it is the one her employer buried.
premises.setting: A commercial tracking station and low orbit, near future.
premises.stakes: Six crew, her clearance, and the difference between debris and a weapon.

premises.protagonist: A 22-year-old archivist on a generation ship is responsible for deleting files to keep the ship's storage under capacity.
premises.situation: One file deletes itself when she opens it and leaves a note addressed to her by name.
premises.conflict: The note describes a fault in the life-support schedule that the ship's council has voted not to record.
premises.setting: A generation ship eleven years into its voyage, no planet in sight.
premises.stakes: The archive, her position, and whether the next cohort is told the truth about the air.

premises.protagonist: A 45-year-old court stenographer has typed every word of the county's trials for eighteen years.
premises.situation: She recognises a transcript she produced: two sentences have been changed, and the change convicts the defendant.
premises.conflict: Her signature is on the certified record, and the man who altered it knows what she did ten years ago.
premises.setting: A county courthouse in a mid-sized American city, present day.
premises.stakes: An innocent man's sentence, her liberty, and the machine she is the only witness to.

premises.protagonist: A 50-year-old retired bomb-disposal officer now trains search dogs and trusts them more than people.
premises.situation: His own dog alerts on a package at his daughter's school, on a day the school is running a lockdown drill.
premises.conflict: The alert is either a hoax aimed at him or the real thing, and clearing the building means admitting publicly what he did in the war.
premises.setting: A suburban town outside a military base, present day.
premises.stakes: Four hundred children, his daughter's opinion of him, and the one call only he can make.
